correctness.rationale: The unit ball satisfies \(x_j^*\le j^{-1/p}\). Rearrangement gives \(\sup_{\|x\|_{p,\infty}\le1}|L_a(x)|=\sum_{j=1}^m a_j^*j^{-1/p}\), and a phase-aligned vector with coordinate moduli \(j^{-1/p}\) attains it. Below the threshold \((m+1)^{-1/p}\), the added coordinate cannot violate any target order-statistic constraint, while the retained coordinates give the reverse norm inequality. Above the threshold, the equality vector forces all \(m+1\) target coordinates above the last threshold, contradicting isometry. The disjointness criterion follows exactly from whether two coordinate basis vectors can share a nonzero added coordinate.

value.rationale: The focal paper uses a single non-surjective isometry to show why surjectivity is structurally important. The new result turns that example into a natural complete classification: the admissible coefficient body is an explicit weighted rearrangement ball, the focal coefficient is exactly extremal, and the same formula separates disjointness-preserving from genuinely support-mixing embeddings. This is a structural boundary for the precise phenomenon motivating the source rather than a routine numerical variant.
